title: Identification and Minimax Estimation of Dose-Response Policies under Quasianalyticity without Positivity
banked_reason: D0.5.G delivered subfield below the field floor: math and rubric panels pass, but the classical quasianalytic branch, broader bounded-Borel modulus, known-design no-covariate scope, and absent quantitative rates cap the paper at 6.7 below the 7.4 field gate.
gap_reasons: The quasianalytic ingredient is the classical uniqueness and cutoff criterion, while polynomial density makes the modulus and risk results apply to the broader bounded-Borel class, limiting the contribution specific to quasianalytic responses.
The known-design, no-covariate model and the absence of finite-sample rates or quantitative fixed-budget bounds constrain the paper’s reach at a leading econometrics journal.
paper_score_ceiling 6.7 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the identification criterion, exact positive-error signed-policy modulus, and sharp asymptotic singular-mass minimax floor; both math and rubric panels passed without findings. The field-tier claim collapsed because the quasianalytic input is classical and the main modulus extends to the broader bounded-Borel Bernoulli class, while quantitative rates, covariates, or unknown- design inference require a genuine re-anchor with new assumptions.
tldr: For known-design Bernoulli dose responses in a local Denjoy--Carleman class, exact identification and uniform estimation have different frontiers. Positive observational error has the exact signed-policy modulus \(c[s+\int_0^{\min(\epsilon/c,1)}w^*(u)\,du]\), and the asymptotic minimax squared-risk floor is \(c^2s^2/4\). Polynomial density makes these two results hold under standard weight growth and even gives the same positive-error and risk formulas for all bounded-Borel Bernoulli curves. Zero-error identification, compact derivative budgets, and pointwise consistency are separate claims.
gap: Classical quasianalyticity controls equality of curves, while causal extrapolation and off-policy research typically use quantitative smoothness or overlap. The joint zero-error and positive-error behavior of arbitrary finite signed policies, including supported singular-continuous mass, is not stated in the inspected primary comparisons.
fill: Investigate the iff identification theorem, exact rearrangement modulus, \(c^2s^2/4\) minimax plateau, and pointwise-versus-uniform distinction in one every-dose Bernoulli model.
